description.summary: The Rake is an internet-born fictional entity originating from 4chan's /b/ board around 2005–2006, described as a pale, emaciated humanoid that crouches at the foot of beds or crawls on all fours. Though explicitly created as collaborative fiction, the character has since generated claimed real-world encounter reports.
description.full: The Rake is a creepypasta character that emerged from 4chan's /b/ board around 2005–2006 as part of a collaborative fictional project aimed at creating a new internet horror entity. It is described as a pale, hairless, emaciated humanoid creature — resembling something between a naked human and a large hairless dog — that crawls on all fours, appears in bedrooms at night crouching at the foot of the bed or standing over sleeping victims, and possesses hollow or blank eyes. The original creepypasta text established a fictional framing device of found documents and journal entries, giving the character a sense of historicity. Like Slender Man (which originated in 2009 on Something Awful), the Rake represents the phenomenon of internet-born fictional entities that acquire reported real-world sightings as the legend spreads. In the 2010s, claimed 'real' encounters with the Rake began circulating online, blurring the documented fictional origin with emerging pseudo-belief. The Rake is distinct from the Polybius legend in having a clearly identifiable fictional creation context, and from older folklore traditions in being purely a product of early internet culture.

etymology.origin: 4chan's /b/ board, approximately 2005–2006. The name 'The Rake' refers to the creature's raking or clawing behavior and emaciated, raked-over appearance.
etymology.meaning: Refers to the entity's clawing/scratching behavior and gaunt, rake-like physique

related_phenomena.name: Slender Man
related_phenomena.description: The most famous internet-born fictional entity that also acquired pseudo-belief reports; Slender Man originated in 2009 on Something Awful

related_phenomena.name: Polybius
related_phenomena.description: Another internet-era urban legend where fiction blurs into claimed real experiences

related_phenomena.name: Shadow People
related_phenomena.description: Older reported bedroom intruder entities that share some phenomenological features with Rake reports

features.description: Completely hairless pale skin, giving a naked, exposed appearance
Extremely thin, skeletal build described as resembling something between a naked man and a large hairless dog
Primarily moves on all fours, though described as able to take a crouching bipedal posture
Eyes are described as hollow, blank, or deeply sunken
Hands end in long, claw-like fingers, consistent with the 'raking' behavior implied by the name

physical.morphology: A pale, hairless, emaciated humanoid that moves primarily on all fours. Proportions are described as wrong for a normal human — too long, too thin, with joints at unnatural angles.

abilities.description: Described as moving silently through homes and into bedrooms without waking occupants
Reportedly crouches at the foot of the bed or over sleeping individuals, watching them
Witnesses in fictional and reported accounts describe overwhelming fear, paralysis, and lasting psychological trauma

patterns: Appears at night in bedrooms of sleeping victims
Crouches at the foot of the bed or over victims
Stares at or watches victims without always attacking
Retreats when noticed in many accounts

range.description: As an internet-born legend, the Rake has no geographic origin. Claimed encounter reports (post-fictional-origin) come primarily from English-speaking internet communities.

peak_activity_periods.description: Creation period and early spread through creepypasta communities
Period when claimed 'real' encounter reports began circulating alongside the established fictional origin

temporal.seasonal_patterns: No seasonal pattern; spread follows internet discussion cycles and horror media trends.

origins.cultural_roots: The Rake was created as a deliberately new piece of internet horror fiction. It draws on older folkloric elements — the bedroom intruder, the watching figure, the pale humanoid — but its specific form was created through collaborative fiction on 4chan's /b/ board around 2005–2006.
origins.earliest_accounts: 4chan /b/ board, approximately 2005–2006. The original fictional framing used fake journal entries and found-document conventions.
origins.folklore_connections: The Rake connects to older traditions of bedroom intruder spirits (hags, night-visitors, shadow people, sleep paralysis demons) and to the broader creepypasta tradition established by Slender Man (2009, Something Awful).

timeline.event: The Rake first appears on 4chan's /b/ board as a collaborative fictional horror project
timeline.significance: Creation of the entity; establishes its documented fictional origin

timeline.event: The Rake spreads to creepypasta wikis and horror communities, gaining a wider internet audience
timeline.significance: Transition from 4chan origin to broader internet legend status

history.modern_era: The Rake continues to circulate as a creepypasta entity, with claimed encounter reports appearing alongside the clearly documented fictional origin. Like Slender Man, it represents the blurring of fiction and pseudo-belief in digital folklore. Unlike Slender Man, the Rake has not yet been linked to real-world incidents of violence.

skeptical.name: Documented fictional creation
skeptical.description: The Rake was explicitly created as collaborative fiction on 4chan approximately 2005–2006. All subsequent 'encounter reports' post-date this creation and are attributable to the spread of the legend rather than genuine encounters with an independent entity.
evidence_cited: Structural identity of 'encounter reports' with the original fictional template
No encounter reports predate the legend's online creation

skeptical.name: Sleep paralysis misattribution
skeptical.description: Claimed 'real' Rake encounters are best explained as sleep paralysis experiences — the hypnagogic hallucination of a figure at the bedside or foot of the bed is well-documented — being interpreted through the template of the Rake legend.
evidence_cited: Sleep paralysis hallucinations of bedroom intruder figures are well-documented neurologically
The Rake's described behavior (crouching at the foot of the bed, watching) matches common sleep paralysis visual hallucinations

traditions: Creepypasta tradition of internet-born horror entities
Found-document horror narrative convention (fictional journal entries, fake case files)
stories: The original 4chan collaborative fiction thread establishing the Rake (approximately 2005–2006)
The spread through Creepypasta Wiki and associated communities
folklore.beliefs: A minority of internet users treat the Rake as a real entity despite its documented fictional origin. This represents a broader pattern in digital folklore where fictional creation blurs into pseudo-belief through repeated uncritical retelling.

film_tv: The Rake has been featured in multiple independent horror short films and YouTube productions
games: The Rake — Roblox game inspired by the legend
Multiple indie horror games use the Rake as an antagonist
other: The Rake is a recurring subject in horror podcast episodes and YouTube documentary channels covering creepypasta history

research.ongoing_studies: The Rake is studied by digital folklorists and internet culture researchers as an example of emergent online legend creation and the mechanisms by which fictional entities acquire pseudo-belief reports.
